title: Pages, the dashboard and getting to know you
summary: The pages Squire makes, the home dashboard and the voice-note pages are all served by one page server on the owner's Mac, and can be seen on that Mac only: another machine cannot connect.

journeys.goal: See a page Squire made, on the owner's own Mac
steps: Squire says a page is ready and gives the link the link command prints at that moment (the address with its secret)
The owner opens the link in their browser on the Mac
The page server serves the page from workspace/pages in the owner's folder, byte for byte as Squire made it

journeys.goal: Open the home dashboard on the owner's own Mac
steps: The owner asks Squire for the dashboard, and Squire gives the link the link command prints at that moment (the address with its secret), or says the pages are not up
The owner opens the link in their browser on the Mac
The page server serves the home dashboard at /, an HTML page of its own

journeys.goal: Leave a comment on a page for Squire to read
steps: The owner opens a page Squire made, on the Mac
The owner picks the words the comment is about and writes the comment in the comment panel
The panel posts it to the page server from the server's own page, with the server's own Origin
The page server keeps the comment in the owner's folder, where Squire reads it as untrusted words, never as the owner's own

navModel.notes: No shared navigation bar and no sign-in: the pages are seen on the owner's Mac only, over the loopback. The home dashboard at / links to the pages; each page under /pages/ is a document served as Squire made it, with the comment panel the server's own; the panel posts to /api/review, which is not a page.
